memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Abraham fell facedown; he laughed and said to himself, "Will a son be born to a man a hundred years old? Will Sarah bear a child at the age of ninety?" - Gen 17:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham's reaction is wonderfully human. He falls facedown in worship - and then he laughs. A hundred years old, a ninety-year-old wife, and a promise of a baby? The sheer impossibility of it strikes him, and something between amazement and disbelief bubbles up. He does the arithmetic and it simply doesn't add up.

We should be gentle in reading this, as God was. Unlike Sarah's later laugh, which God gently questioned, Abraham's laugh here is not condemned. It seems to be the laughter of a man staggered by a promise too big to fit inside his understanding - faith and astonishment tangled together. Even the great man of faith found God's promise almost too much to take in.

There is comfort in this for us. Faith is not always calm and composed. Sometimes God's promises are so far beyond our reckoning that we can only laugh at the wonder of them. Believing does not mean we stop being amazed; often the deepest faith is the most amazed.

And there is a lovely detail: the son would be named Isaac, meaning "he laughs." God would take Abraham's astonished laughter and turn it into the child's very name - laughter transformed into joy. Paul says Abraham "did not waver through unbelief... but was strengthened in his faith" (Rom 4:20). Bring your staggered, amazed, barely-able-to-believe faith to God. He can work with that.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do God's promises ever seem too big to take in?
- Can you bring even your amazed, half-disbelieving faith to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, sometimes Your promises are so vast I can hardly take them in. Thank You that You receive even my astonished, staggering faith. Turn my amazement into joy, as You did for Abraham.
Amen.
